cover: real next-token probabilities from Qwen3-0.6B after "Generative AI: from chat to" (demo/title_next.py, demo/title_rank.py, 11 Oct 2026): code 7.5%, AI 2.4%, content 1.9%; " agents" 0.006%, rank 1,462.

the race is an illustration, not a measurement: the clocks are made up to show the pattern; person B's steps match the demo data (demo/live/loans.csv has 8 duplicate rows).

real run: demo/enter_demo.py → demo/enter-demo.json (Qwen3-0.6B, thinking off, greedy, 11 Oct 2026). The chat format is Qwen3's real template (tokenizer.apply_chat_template); with thinking off it also adds an empty <think></think> block, not shown. The answer really starts "Certainly! Here's a cleaned and summarized version of the CSV data…": the model has no file.

real run: Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer on my laptop (scratchpad nexttok.py)

real run: Qwen3-0.6B, greedy (always the top token); data in demo/lm-data.json, made by demo/lm_steps.py

real logits from Qwen3-0.6B for the 12 likeliest next tokens (of ~150,000), renormalised; demo/temperature-logits.json. Two rounds of six draws: temperature 1.0 and 0.3. Top-p (cut the long tail before the draw) is not shown; mention if asked.

note: the previous slide used greedy decoding (always the likeliest), which is why it ended in the French Alps every time.

schematic: the guesses and counts are illustrative; real pre-training sets are tens of trillions of tokens

Base-model email: real run, Qwen3-0.6B-Base, greedy, wrote a long email (scratchpad chatdemo/probe.py, 11 Oct 2026). Assistant paradigm: Askell et al., "A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment", Anthropic, arXiv 2112.00861 (Dec 2021): HHH and the Human/Assistant dialogue format; then Bai et al., "Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with RLHF", arXiv 2204.05862 (Apr 2022); Constitutional AI: Bai et al., arXiv 2212.08073 (Dec 2022).

sources: Constitutional AI: Bai et al., "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback", Anthropic, arXiv 2212.08073 (Dec 2022). In practice step 2 = supervised fine-tuning on example conversations (here the answers ARE written down) + preference grading by people or an AI grader (RLHF/RLAIF, via a reward model). Step 3 = reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

sources: anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5 (22 Sep 2026); openai.com (6 Aug 2026); indiatoday.in (5 Oct 2026)

schematic; the 28 layers are Qwen3-0.6B's. Bigger models have more and wider layers.

real run: Qwen3-0.6B, attention of "it", averaged over heads (demo/attention_weights.py → demo/attn.json). The first token soaks up most attention in every model (an "attention sink"), so it is faded and left out of the arcs.

source: arcprize.org/leaderboard (checked 11 Oct 2026). ARC-AGI-3 Standard harness: GPT-6 Astra (Max) 62.7%, $26.1K; GPT-6.1 Sol (Max) 52.7%, $7.6K; Claude Opus 5 (High) 30.2%, $20.7K; Gemini 3.8 Flash (High) 10.4%, $4.4K; Claude Opus 5.5: not run on ARC-AGI-3. "Provider Adapter" runs: Astra 98.6%, Sol 96.2%. ARC-AGI-2: Opus 5.5 (High) 93.3%, Astra (Max) 95.0%. Human leaderboard: top players solve all 25 games. arcprize.org/arc-agi/3: "A 100% score means AI agents can beat every game as efficiently as humans." Launch score (Gemini 3.1 Pro 0.37%, March 2026): presenc.ai ARC-AGI tracker.

Index = Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2, max (or highest available) effort. Sources: anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5; artificialanalysis.ai model pages (GPT-6.1 Sol max 52, $2/$10; GPT-6 Luna max 38; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 39, $0.30/$1.20 on DeepSeek's API); artificialanalysis.ai/articles/gemini-4-argon-google-top-three-labs (30 Sep 2026: Argon high 53, 12 points ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash high → 41; Argon at a 50% launch discount); venturebeat.com (22 Sep 2026: Luna $0.10/$0.50, MiMo-V2.6-Pro $0.435/$0.87, Gemini 3.8 Flash $0.75/$3.75 until 31 Dec, GLM-5.3 $1.40/$4.40); eesel.ai (Astra pricing). Sonnet 5.5: $2 / $10 (anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5 pricing table, Oct 2026). Haiku 5.5: released 7 Oct 2026, $0.10 / $0.50 for prompts up to 100k tokens, $0.50 / $2.50 above (anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5); index 43 at max effort (artificialanalysis.ai/articles/claude-sonnet-5-5, 7 Oct 2026; 38 at high effort).

Index: Artificial Analysis v4.3.2, max (or highest available) effort (Oct 2026). Price: $ per million output tokens: Anthropic and OpenAI list prices; GPT-6.1 Sol and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash from their artificialanalysis.ai pages; Luna, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, Gemini 3.8 Flash (introductory, until 31 Dec) and GLM-5.3 from venturebeat.com (22 Sep 2026); Kimi K3 on OpenRouter; Sonnet 5.5 from third-party trackers; Gemini 3.8 Flash index = Argon 53 − 12 (artificialanalysis.ai, 30 Sep 2026). Gemini 4 Argon left out: launch discount, no stable price. Price per token is not cost per task: bigger models may need fewer tokens.

He also mentions the 722 manuscripts in openai/math.

data: demo/live/loans.csv, made by demo/make_live_data.py from OpenML "credit-g" (1,000 loans, 30% defaulted). Problems added on purpose, listed only in make_live_data.py (not in the demo folder, so the agent cannot read them): 8 duplicated rows, 25 missing ages, 12 credit amounts typed as text such as "3,338 CHF".
